identity: Original (untranslated) Arabic scholarly art-history prose: a book chapter titled 'al-Fann al-Tuluni wa-Samarra' on Tulunid art in Egypt and its derivation from Abbasid Samarra. Early-to-mid 20th-century Egyptian academic register (Zaki Muhammad Hasan school), Hindawi-style reprint. Learned first-person-plural voice ('wa-naqsudu bi-dhalika', 'wa-lasna naqsudu', 'wa-nahnu'), heavy nominal predication, a roster of European orientalists glossed in Latin script, and long periodic sentences built out of coordinated finite clauses. By my LAW 6 table this is the encyclopedic/expository band (sections B/I/L in my doctrine), my strongest register, target sentence 12-20 tokens; LAW 1 applies at full strength and only section H (confessional memoir) would invert it, which this is not.
law: The gold reconstructs the ORIGINAL INK, not the sense (LAW 0). Operative rules here: (1) waw + a fresh finite clause carrying a NEW ARGUMENT (new subject, new topic NP, or a new heavy object in this expository register) = CUT; waw joining bare nouns, adjectives or adjunct phrases inside one clause = NEVER cut. (2) Resumptive fa- opening a new explanatory move = CUT (fa-al-mithaluna, fa-yuqalu, fa-qad, fa-nahnu). (3) Very short verdict clauses stand alone (wa-la ghurwa, wa-hadha za'mun ghayru sahih) - doctrine C2. (4) A trailing subordinate (alladhi, hina, hatta, in lam, kama, bi-dalili) belongs to the clause before it - LAW 4, do NOT cut before it. (5) hayth opens its own segment - doctrine B2/K2. (6) A protasis+apodosis is ONE unit (C1) when the protasis is short, but a 16-token fronted protasis takes a comma in print and therefore cuts. (7) A comma-bracketed parenthetical yields TWO boundaries, not zero - doctrine B5. (8) A display enumeration of full referential NPs (proper names, titles) cuts at every item, because Arabic prints such rosters comma-separated and the annotators fragment name blocks brutally (A1/A2: 'Robert L || Rothstein and Daniel D || Perlmutter'); a set of bare coordinated nouns inside a clause does not (B5 kept 'afradan wa-duwalan wa-mu'assasat dawliyya' whole). Target density about 14 tokens per sentence in running prose.
reasoning: CALIBRATION FIRST (checklist item 1). First 200 tokens run: nominal thesis (5 tok) / waw+clause (7) / fa-clause (16) / waw+clause (27) / waw+clause (9) / lakinna-clause (19). That is the section B rhythm, not section H, so LAW 1 fires and my old welding default stays off. || THE BIG BET - the orientalist roster @324-352. Twelve items each headed by waw: kurbit CORBETT, wa-fan barsham VAN BERCHEM, wa-salmun SALMON, wa-hirtz basha HERZ PACHA, wa-saladan SALADIN, wa-zarrih SARRE, wa-hirtzfild HERZFELD, wa-shtrijufski STRZYGOWSKI, wa-fluri FLURY, wa-krizul CRESWELL, wa-akkush, wa-hutkir HAUTECOEUR, wa-fiyit WIET. Two doctrines collide. LAW 1's exception says phrase-level waw is NEVER cut. Against that: (a) LAW 0's corollary that the comma often became a boundary, and an Arabic roster of thirteen names is printed comma-separated; (b) section A1/A2 shows the annotators shred name blocks at every reconstructed mark rather than protecting them; (c) doc_c188bbc9702e @40 cut before a bare waw joining two book titles; (d) LAW 0 says cut at a coin flip and my base rate is 4.8:1 under-cutting. I resolve the collision with a limiter: an enumeration of FULL REFERENTIAL NPs (names, titles) cuts; an enumeration of bare nouns or adjunct phrases inside a clause does not. That keeps B5's 'afradan wa-duwalan' whole while cutting the roster. Cost is symmetric (about 11 boundaries either way in a ~45-boundary document), so LAW 0 breaks the tie toward cutting. Marked lo throughout - this is the one decision that could swing the document. Same limiter applied at @89/91/93 (fann amawi, wa-fann abbasi, wa-fann tuluni - coined style-labels after a colon, display enumeration, cut, lo) but NOT at @28/30 (ijabatan li-talabihi wa-tahqiqan li-raghbatihi wa-ishba'an li-shahawatihi - parallel masdar adjuncts inside one clause, exactly B5's protected shape), NOT at @44 (bilatihi wa-hashiyatihi aw fi al-usar - alternative PPs), NOT at @561-564 (al-ustadhayn zarrih SARRE wa-hirtzfild HERZFELD - a two-item pair, no comma in Arabic print, matching the un-cut internal waw of 'wa-kaslan jiddan wal-asad'). || @58 and @67: 'wa-lasna naqsudu... wa-lakinna naqulu...' is the classic not-X-but-Y pair. The lakinna clause is 19 tokens with wholly new content, so by T2's hypothesis (over ~6 tokens with new content = head, not tail) it is a head and gets its own segment. Logging this for T2. Same call at @162 (9-token lakinnahu clause, cut) and @423 (31-token lakinnana clause, cut). All three push T2 toward the length discriminator. || @171/@173: 'wa-la ghurwa' is a two-token verdict clause. Doctrine C2 ('wa-huwa batil ||', three tokens, its own segment) is a direct precedent for cutting BEFORE it. Cutting AFTER it, before 'fa-qad istata'a', is the shakier half - T4 says causal fa after a NEGATED clause welds, and 'la ghurwa' is negated. But C2 says the short verdict stands alone on both sides and LAW 2 says resumptive fa cuts. Cut, marked lo, logged against T4. || @203: cut before hayth. LAW 4 would protect a trailing subordinate, but B2 (doc_47764cf032d7 @762) and K2 (doc_c567a2257203 @27) both record gold cutting before hayth in expository/news prose. Two independent confirmations beat the general rule. || @247: 'mustaqillun fi al-tarikh al-fanni li-Misr, lahu sifatuhu wa-mumayyizatuhu' - an appositive predicate set off by a comma. G2 says apposition cuts even where clause-chaining welds. Lo. || @269/@284: a two-protasis, one-apodosis period (in kana al-fann al-fatimi... wa-in kana fann al-mamalik... fa-inna al-fann al-tuluni...). C1 says every conditional period is its own sentence; welding all three gives a 53-token monster, three times the register. Cut at both joints. || @381/@393: 'lam yakuna min al-hamaj al-mutawahhishin, bal kana min al-qaba'il..., wa-waritha al-fann al-siti'. Two commas in print. The waw at @394 shares its subject with what precedes, which in section E would ride along (fa-jalasa wa-akala khubzan), BUT section L records exactly this shape - wa-tashmulu, wa-hiya, wal-fa'ida, same subject, new heavy object - as gold cuts I kept absorbing. Expository register overrides the narrative VP-chain exemption. Cut. || @401/@405: 'wa-hadha za'mun ghayru sahih' is C4 (waw + new topic NP with nominal predicate) AND C2 (four-token verdict standing alone), so it is fenced on both sides; the following 'fa-nahnu nusallimu' is textbook LAW 2. Both hi. || @466/@482: 'fa-qad arafa al-fann al-islami fi Misr fi ahd al-fatimiyyin - wa-hum laysu min al-jins al-hindi al-uruubi alladhi ghalabat alayhi al-sibgha al-turkiyya ala haddi qawli fun Lukuk - taqadduman wa-izdihar'. A dash/comma-bracketed parenthetical splitting a verb from its object. B5 is explicit: this becomes TWO boundaries, not zero. This is the site I would have missed in batch 1. || THE FRONTED-ADVERBIAL / APODOSIS-FA CALL, made consistently four times. C1 says protasis+apodosis is one unit, and LAW 4's mirror case ('ala ma yabdu' attaching forward with no boundary after it) says a short sentence adverbial welds to what follows. So NO cut after the short fronted openers: 'wa-nahnu idh istathnayna al-sultan' (4 tok) before fa-lan @36, 'wa-idhan' before fa-laysa @99, 'wa-fadlan an dhalika' (3 tok) before fa-qad @458, 'wa-mahma yakun min shay'' (4 tok) before fa-inna @508. But at @618 the protasis 'wa-idh innana sanudtarru fi kathirin min al-ahwal ila al-iltija' ila hadhihi al-asima li-natafahhama usul al-zakharif al-tuluniyya' runs 16 tokens - a fronted clause that long takes a comma in print - so I cut before 'fa-innahu yajduru bina'. Length is the discriminator; it fires exactly once. Marked lo. || @532: cut before 'wa-khassatan fi Samarra'. Phrase-level waw argues against, but 504-548 unbroken is 45 tokens against a 12-20 register, and a comma before wa-khassatan is near-certain. LAW 0 breaks the tie. Lo. || SITES I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CUT, applying LAW 4 and LAW 5's look-one-joint-earlier check: before 'kama kanat tatba'uha fi al-siyasa' @111 (comparative adjunct trailing its main clause, not J7's additive kama); before 'in lam yafuqhu abbahatan wa-azamatan' @187; before 'alladhi kana yahrisu' @584 (LAW 4 forbids cutting before a trailing alladhi even with a comma); before 'hina zahara Ahmad ibn Tulun' @541; before 'bi-dalili ma wasala ilayna' @488 and its coordinate 'wa-ma katabahu al-Maqrizi' @496 (two ma-clauses as complements of one preposition - phrase-level, not a referential enumeration, so my roster limiter does not reach it); inside 'asima al-khilafa al-abbasiyya' @301 (tight appositive of a place name, no comma). || DENSITY CHECK: 57 boundaries over 625 non-NL tokens = 11.0 tokens per segment; excluding the 12 roster cuts, 45 boundaries = 13.9 tokens per segment, squarely inside the 12-20 encyclopedic band.
